subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Definition of Done
description: A 60-second lesson on Definition of Done.

hook.text: 'Is it done?' The developer says yes. The tester says no. The PM says maybe. They need a shared definition.

buildup.text: Definition of Done (DoD) is a team agreement listing criteria a feature must meet before it's considered complete.

discovery.text: A typical DoD: coded, reviewed, tested, documented, and deployed to staging. Everyone knows the bar.

twist.text: Without DoD, 'done' means whatever each person wants it to mean. That leads to bugs and rework.

climax.text: Teams with a clear DoD reduce escaped defects by 30% because nothing ships without meeting the checklist.

punchline.text: If everyone agrees what 'done' means, fewer things ship broken.

quiz.question: What problem does a Definition of Done solve?
options: Ambiguity about when a feature is truly complete
